title: Ordinary cohomology comparison on arbitrary augmented injective rows
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $G,G\prime$ abelian etale sheaves on $X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $R,R\prime$ nonnegative injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and $v:f^*G\to G\prime$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. A row comparison $\phi:f^*R\to R\prime$ intertwines the degree-zero augmentations with $v$. Apply the global-sections pullback unit degreewise and then $\phi$ to form ceRowSectionsMap [lem-weil-pbc-ce-total-sections-comparison]. For each $p\in\mathbb N$, the isomorphism ceRowOrdinaryIso from homology of sections of the row to $H^p(X,G)$ is explicitly the inverse of Ext/resolution evaluation at 1, transported through extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-ext-resolution-sections-iso]. Its square with the homology map of ceRowSectionsMap and the composite $H^p(v)\circ\mathrm{cohomologyMap}(f,G,p)$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] commutes. The construction cePresentationRow packages the actual terms and augmentation of a given CE presentation, without choosing data.

proof.text: Extend the two nonnegative injective rows and their comparison by zero. The canonical map-extend comparison identifies the resulting sections map with the extension of ceRowSectionsMap. Compute Ext pullback on a cocycle from the constant integer sheaf, then compose with the coefficient map. The augmentation equation identifies this with the cocycle of the supplied row comparison: compare with the chosen resolution of the pulled-back sheaf, use injectivity of the target to lift the coefficient map, and use uniqueness of augmentation-compatible comparisons up to homotopy. This uses no injectivity of the pulled-back row.

Evaluation at 1 commutes with inverse image via the constant-sheaf transpose and with postcomposition via the adjunction. It therefore identifies the Ext cocycle map with the sections row map. Coboundaries map to coboundaries. Descend to homology and transport through mapExtendIso and extendHomologyIso; expand the explicit ceRowOrdinaryIso. The square holds in degree zero as well, and for zero sheaves and empty schemes.

theorem ceRowOrdinaryIso_naturality {X Y : Scheme.{uNatural}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{uNatural + 1})
    (G' : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{uNatural + 1})
    (R : InjectiveResolution G) (R' : InjectiveResolution G')
    (v : (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{uNatural + 1} f).obj G ⟶ G')
    (φ : ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{uNatural + 1} f).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj R.cocomplex ⟶ R'.cocomplex)
    (hφ : (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{uNatural + 1} f).map
        ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 G).inv ≫ R.ι.f 0) ≫
          φ.f 0 =
      v ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 G').inv ≫ R'.ι.f 0)
    (p : ℕ) :
    HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (ceRowSectionsMap f φ) p ≫
        (ceRowOrdinaryIso Y G' R' p).hom =
      (ceRowOrdinaryIso X G R p).hom ≫
        AddCommGrpCat.ofHom ((Sheaf.H.map v p).comp (cohomologyMap f G p))
